697fb953-ecb3-4a54-832b-7055d4559df1.quote: Dawn opened with first blood, Terra onto Crunch at 1.7 minutes, and three lanes ran clean the whole game: Steel shut out Sevarog, Kira never lost to Drongo, and Aurora held an early jungle edge over Khaimera. The exception was mid, where Neon lost to Gideon from start to finish; Gideon finished with the match's biggest damage total (68k, per the counter-build read) while only one dawn hero itemized magic resist against him. That mid deficit showed up on the map — river fights went 2-26 in dusk's favor and towers finished 2-10 — and it kept compounding through the fights: dawn won six fights outright across the game but converted none of them into a tower or objective, while dusk cashed five of their seven wins. The two most expensive losses, the 10.4-minute fight near their Fangtooth and the 16.3-minute teamfight at their Inner Tower, both had an alive teammate who wasn't losing their lane sitting out while the rest fought and lost by three-plus bodies. The 18.8-minute and 26.8-minute fights were then started with the midlaner still pinned in that losing lane — the wrong calls to make with a fifth already stuck across the map. The game ended at 29.6 minutes with the full roster in a straight fight at the enemy's Core that went 0-5 — no rotation issue there, just a fight lost outright. Next game: when a teammate is alive and not losing their lane, get them into the fight before it starts, not after — both of the costliest losses had exactly that gap open.
